_about: Every number the verdict uses lives here. status 'cited' means a published source; 'measured' means the author's own benchmark. Edit a value and the verdict follows.

skip_retrieval_tokens.unit: estimated tokens in the whole vault
skip_retrieval_tokens.source: Anthropic, 'Introducing Contextual Retrieval': a knowledge base smaller than about 200,000 tokens (roughly 500 pages) can go straight into the prompt with no retrieval step.

recommended_tokens.unit: estimated tokens in the whole vault
recommended_tokens.source: Mason's benchmark for the video (Claude Sonnet, one fictional company's Obsidian-style vault, 36 questions x 3 runs per arm, 100 to 50,000 notes). From 1,000 notes up, browsing used a median of 33,000 to 51,000 tokens per notes question and injection saved 17,000 to 27,000 of them. The 5M line is a judgment between the 746k-token and 7.6M-token test sizes. Results are not public yet.

bm25_crossover_tokens.source: arXiv 2607.26497, 'BM25 Wins at Scale': plain keyword (BM25) retrieval overtook a file-browsing agent around 10M corpus tokens, while dense embedding retrieval did no better than the agent at full scale. That study used a small open model; Mason's benchmark, with Claude Sonnet, saw no accuracy crossover up to about 38M tokens.
